source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Pr 7:1-27 . The subject continued, by a delineation of the arts of strange women, as a caution to the unwary.

entries.heading: 2. apple . . . eye
entries.text: 2. apple . . . eye --pupil of eye, a custody ( Pr 4:23 ) of special value.

entries.heading: 3. Bind . . . fingers
entries.text: 3. Bind . . . fingers --as inscriptions on rings.
5. The design of the teaching (compare Pr 2:16; 6:24 ).

entries.heading: 6. For
entries.text: 6. For --or, "Since," introducing an example to illustrate the warning, which, whether a narrative or a parable, is equally pertinent. window --or, "opening" looked --literally, "watched earnestly" ( Jud 5:28 ). casement --or, "lattice."

entries.heading: 7. simple
entries.text: 7. simple --as in Pr 1:4 . void of, &c.--(Compare Pr 6:32 ).

entries.heading: 8. her corner
entries.text: 8. her corner --where she was usually found. went . . . house --implying, perhaps, confidence in himself by his manner, as denoted in the word went --literally, "tread pompously."
9. The time, twilight, ending in darkness. black . . . night --literally, "pupil," or, "eye," that is, middle of night.

entries.heading: 10. attire
entries.text: 10. attire --that of harlots was sometimes peculiar. subtile --or, "wary," "cunning."

entries.heading: 11, 12. loud
entries.text: 11, 12. loud --or, "noisy," "bustling." stubborn --not submissive. without . . . streets, . . . corner --(Compare 1Ti 5:13; Tit 2:5 ).

13-15. The preparations for a feast do not necessarily imply peculiar religious professions. The offerer retained part of the victim for a feast ( Le 3:9 , &c.). This feast she professes was prepared for him whom she boldly addresses as one sought specially to partake of it.

entries.heading: 16, 17. my bed
entries.text: 16, 17. my bed --or, "couch," adorned in the costliest manner.

entries.heading: 17. bed
entries.text: 17. bed --a place for sleeping.
18-20. There is no fear of discovery.

entries.heading: 20. the day appointed
entries.text: 20. the day appointed --perhaps, literally, "a full moon," that is, a fortnight's time (compare Pr 7:19 ).

entries.heading: 21. caused . . . yield
entries.text: 21. caused . . . yield --or, "inclines." flattering --(Compare Pr 5:3 ). forced him --by persuasion overcoming his scruples.

entries.heading: 22. straightway
entries.text: 22. straightway --quickly, either as ignorant of danger, or incapable of resistance.

entries.heading: 23. Till
entries.text: 23. Till --He is now caught ( Pr 6:26 ).
24. The inferential admonition is followed ( Pr 7:26, 27 ), by a more general allegation of the evils of this vice.
26, 27. Even the mightiest fail to resist her deathly allurements.
